chunks: And the one who narrated it: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Dharih al-Muharibi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Umrah followed by Hajj (Tamattu') and was prevented (from completing Hajj) after entering the state of Ihram, what should he do? He said: 'Did he stipulate upon his Lord before entering Ihram that He should release him from his Ihram when an obstacle presented itself to him from the affairs of Allah?' I said: 'Yes, he did stipulate that.' He said: 'Then let him return to his people in a state of freedom (from Ihram), for there is no Ihram upon him, for Allah is more entitled to fulfill what was stipulated upon Him.' I said: 'And is Hajj obligatory upon him next year?' He said: 'No.'

The meaning of this is for the one whose Hajj is voluntary (supererogatory), for if he is prevented, Hajj is not obligatory upon him for the next year. And the previous narrations include the one whose Hajj is the Hajj of Islam (obligatory), for he is obligated to perform Hajj the next year, according to what we have presented. And the one performing Umrah should stipulate upon his Lord that He should release him wherever he is detained, and similarly the one who is Mufrid (for Hajj) as well, if it is not an obligatory Hajj, but a voluntary Umrah, that was narrated.

key_terms.الْمُفْرِدُ: The one performing Mufrid (solely for Hajj)
key_terms.حِلًّا: In a state of freedom (from Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who is prevented from completing Hajj after entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition of *shart* (stipulation) required for a pilgrim in *Tamattu'* to be exempt from returning for Hajj if prevented (*muhsar*) after entering Ihram. Al-Tusi’s commentary distinguishes this from the obligatory Hajj of Islam, which remains due even if voluntary, emphasizing that the stipulation must be made prior to entering the state of Ihram to ensure valid release.
